page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The memory configuration comprises 32 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is provided via an integrated 937 GB NVMe SSD. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, and baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps.

The underlying Intel processor incorporates 320 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and instruction set support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Performance benchmarks reflect top-tier single-core execution, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 alongside strong single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression throughput. Conversely, multi-threaded CPU throughput registers lower relative to the broader market, constrained by the 2 physical core configuration. In data layer benchmarks, the instance delivers 6.18 million Redis SET operations per second and standard database test results.

From an architectural standpoint, the platform couples dense local NVMe storage and high memory allocation against a modest 2 Gbps baseline network pipe and limited parallel compute threads. Combining DDR5 memory with direct NVMe storage provides qualitative resource efficiency for localized I/O operations without relying on network-attached block devices. The i7i.xlarge fits transactional databases, NoSQL key-value stores, in-memory caching layers, and local I/O-bound processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, delivering substantial memory capacity and direct-attached NVMe storage. It features 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 2 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz, paired with 32 GB of DDR5 memory and a 937 GB local NVMe SSD. Hardware accelerators include Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, while dedicated GPUs are omitted. Benchmark metrics highlight top-tier single-core processing speed and robust single-threaded compression performance, counterbalanced by modest multi-threaded throughput due to the core count limit. Networking baseline throughput is 2 Gbps. This server profile offers efficient local I/O and memory density without external storage overhead, making it functional for relational databases, Redis caching layers, NoSQL stores, and localized transactional workloads.
